title: Ground truth: hardening, compliance, real tests and staging
rule: Only a passing test or a completed acceptance run flips `passes` to true. Tests are never edited to pass.

features.statement: Model profiles route aliases per profile and a price table prices usage
A per-day test budget guard caps spend and rolls with the day
Outreach to a suppressed address or domain, or without a sender identity, is blocked at the gate
Every first-contact email carries the footer, List-Unsubscribe and List-Unsubscribe-Post
GET or POST /u/{token} writes an opt-out suppression and never redirects; bad tokens answer 404
Bounces and opt-out replies mark the lead and write a suppression
The founder saves the sender identity in Settings; without it a batch is blocked with a readable reason
The fence blocks any external action whose target is outside the allow-lists, default deny
No agent subprocess receives the model key, HOME or the host config; each company has its own config dir
Engineering runs under the SDK sandbox with unsandboxed commands refused and a network allow-list
The gateway injects the key, strips the caller's, streams SSE unchanged and refuses past the cap
Record then replay serves the stored response without the upstream; a miss fails readably
Agent session entries persist append-only and never reach the browser
Memory items are embedded inside Supabase and searched hybrid (full text + vector, RRF)
Memory enters runs as bounded data: digest capped at 8,000 chars, search results in a stripped, capped block
The Meta adapter targets Graph API v26.0
Real-Claude smoke runs on every PR under $0.50 on the smoke profile
Staging (Vercel, Supabase, Fly, Inngest) passes the staging check: fence on, env staging, sandbox routes closed, buckets private
The nightly staging journey runs green from the workflow
Milestone acceptance on the production profile: real magic link, onboarding with real Claude, artifacts open, kill switch within 5 s, cost at most $10
The gap report lists what the acceptance proved weak and what M8 fixes first
